title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
blurb: Eric Ries argues that most startups fail not because they can't build a product, but because they build something nobody wants. Drawing on his own experience, including the early struggles of the company IMVU, he proposes a scientific approach to entrepreneurship. A startup, he says, is any team creating something new under extreme uncertainty, whether in a garage or inside a large corporation. Instead of writing detailed plans, founders should treat their vision as a set of assumptions to test. They build a minimum viable product, measure how real customers respond, and learn whether to stay the course or pivot. Progress is measured by validated learning, not by vanity numbers. The book's core engine is the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop, and the goal is to move through it as fast as possible, wasting less time, money, and effort.
